messages:
rafa_global: Quick question 30 relocating to Berlin next month and need to move my benefits for my spouse + 11mo to EU coverage. My start date there is 2026-04-01. How do we handle mid-year change, premium proration, and any payroll tax paperwork? Dont want a gap in coverage.

emily_benefits: Congrats on the move, @rafa_global! Youre eligible for a QLE for change of residence. Please submit the QLE with your relocation date (2026-04-01) and indicate desired effective date. We can switch benefits to our EU carrier effective 2026-04-01.

john_payroll: Payroll note: premiums are prorated by payroll period. If youre moving mid-pay-period we usually prorate to the date-of-change. Also let us know if you want premiums taken in local currency or remain USD net-pay conversion (we support both for certain payroll runs).

rafa_global: Thanks. Two related things: 1) my spouse is currently on domestic dental + vision heres the plan codes: MED-DOM-1 / DENT-STD. Will those map cleanly to EU equivalents? 2) Is there any tax reporting I need to worry about for dependent coverage changes when we have a foreign address?

emily_benefits: 1) We have mapped equivalents: EU-MED-1 and EU-DENT-CORE. But benefits levels may differ (copays, networks). Well send plan comparison. If you want to elect a different tier (e.g., family vs employee+child) choose that on the QLE form.

benefits-bot: QLE link: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle  select "Relocation" and attach proof (work visa or relocation paperwork) + dependent docs. Deadline: 60 days from the event (residency change).

john_payroll: 2) For US tax reporting: employer-sponsored coverage for foreign dependents is generally not taxable, but payroll tax treatment can vary by country. If you switch to EU payroll deductions, local social contributions may apply. Looping @tax-legal to confirm cross-border withholding.

rafa_global: I may be on contractor payroll in Germany for first 3 months. If benefits are billed to company but Im paid locally as contractor, will that break eligibility?

tax-legal: Hi @rafa_global  short answer: possibly. Eligibility and tax treatment depends on whether you remain on Redwood payroll or are on a local contractor arrangement. If benefits are provided while not on company payroll, they could be treated as taxable income locally. Please DM your relocation PM and well pull your employment status.

emily_benefits: If youre contractor-payrolled for a period, we can still enroll dependents but need a signed statement from People Ops and payroll confirming employer-sponsored coverage. It adds an extra sign-off step.

rafa_global: Understood. Also how will premium proration appear on my payslip? Example: last US pay in March covering 3/16-3/31 and relocation on 4/1.

john_payroll: Good example. If your last US pay covers 3/16-3/31, and EU coverage starts 4/1, US premiums will stop on 3/31. Any overlapping premiums charged in error will be refunded as payroll credit. If coverage change occurs mid-pay period we compute daily prorate:

    Overpaid = (US premium per day) * (days after effective date in current pay period)

We show an adjustment line item and reason code "BEN-QLE-PRORATE" on the stub.

emily_benefits: Well also produce new insurance ID cards for EU plans and notify carriers. For the child under 12 months, make sure birth cert is uploaded and passport/visa if applicable.

rafa_global: Great. Timeline: Ill submit QLE today with relocation docs. If tax-legal flags anything, ping me. Want to avoid surprise withholding before April.

tax-legal: Please attach your tentative payroll status (employee v contractor) and local contract start date. Well respond within 2 business days.

emily_benefits: Case opened: RL-2026-1122. Ill DM you the case link and add plan comparisons.

rafa_global: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick help. :raised_hands:
